summary: The clearest story in the data is the PDH Breakout panel at 0% win rate across 23 signals — 18 losses, 5 expired — which points to a structural problem, not a threshold issue: the panel fires on any fresh PDH close with RSI≥60 and EMA above, but has no gate preventing entries into overbought, high-RSI breakouts that immediately fade back. The Exhaustion Short missed-signals analysis shows all 7 misses were blocked by a single gate (prev_day_rally threshold of 6%), with actual moves of −6.21% to +1.75% — meaning large intraday selloffs are being caused by earnings/news exhaustion that has nothing to do with prior-day rally size, so that gate needs structural loosening plus a cumulative-rally fallback anchor. The Bull Trap Reversal panel at 4.3% win rate (1W/7L/15E) is firing too freely with no check that the failed breakout candle itself was a high-volume false spike — the current code only checks the reversal candle's volume, not the trap candle's, allowing weak breakouts that never really trapped anyone to qualify.

proposals.reasoning: All 7 missed signals over 30 days were blocked exclusively by the prev_day_rally gate. The sample shows actual prev-day rally values of +1.75% (SIEMENS, fell 5.09%), +1.38% (HINDUNILVR, fell 8.72%), +0.23% (DMART, fell 6.02%), −0.87% (BANDHANBNK, fell 7.32%), −6.21% (BANDHANBNK again, fell 5.72%). The average actual fall was 6.26%. A threshold of 6.0% categorically excludes stocks that fall sharply on earnings, news, or valuation reset — exactly the high-conviction exhaustion shorts. The gate was designed to confirm prior bullish exhaustion, but real exhaustion selling also fires from consolidation tops and news gaps. Reducing to 2.0% still requires some net positive prior-day move while capturing the missed signals where actual_value ranged from 1.38% to 1.75%.
proposals.expected_impact: Directly recovers the 7 missed signals (avg fall 6.26%) blocked by this gate. Will increase raw signal count; the cumul_rally_pct check (EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT) still acts as a secondary anchor since both conditions must fail together to reject — lowering this threshold means single-day 2%+ moves qualify even without cumulative buildup.

proposals.reasoning: The logic rejects a stock only if BOTH prev_day_rally_pct < EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT AND cumul_rally_pct < EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT. After lowering EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT to 2.0, the cumulative gate becomes the gating factor for stocks with flat or slightly positive prior-day moves. BANDHANBNK on 2026-07-23 had prev_day = −6.21% (well below any threshold) — it only passes through if cumul_rally_pct ≥ threshold. A 3-day cumulative of 5% is a reasonable sign of a topping cluster. Keeping the cumulative gate at 12% means the pair together still blocks too aggressively — a stock up 4% over 3 days then down 0.5% yesterday should qualify for exhaustion short given the right spike candle.
proposals.expected_impact: Working in tandem with the EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT reduction, this recovers the missed signals where a modest multi-day rally (5–12% cumulative) preceded a large intraday selloff. Risk: may increase false positives on stocks that are genuinely recovering from a dip rather than exhausting — the 5-min spike candle and volume gates remain as quality filters.

proposals.title: Add ATR-relative distance-from-PDH gate to reject overextended entries
proposals.proposed_change: After the existing EMA and RSI gates, and before the volume gate, add a new gate: compute the 14-period ATR on daily closes (using the standard Wilder true-range method, same as the existing RSI helper pattern), then reject any signal where (current_price − pdh) / atr14_daily > PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR. Suggested constant PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR = 0.5, meaning the price at signal time must be within 0.5× the daily ATR above PDH. Stocks that have already extended more than half an ATR beyond PDH have priced in the breakout — late entries are where the 18 losses are most likely clustering. Add to the result dict as 'atr14_daily' and 'stretch_atr' for display. Gate code: stretch_atr = (current_price - pdh) / atr14_daily; if stretch_atr > PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR: _dbg_fail(...); continue.
proposals.reasoning: PDH Breakout has 0 wins in 23 signals (0% win rate, 18 outright losses). The current logic has no gate on how far price has already moved past PDH before the signal fires. With RSI≥60 already filtering for momentum stocks, the breakout bar itself plus up to 3 stale bars (_PDH_FRESH=3, 45 min of drift) means the screener is routinely handing entries 1–2% above the actual breakout level, which is above any rational structural SL. An ATR-distance cap forces entries to be close to the structural level where the SL actually makes sense. This is the most likely single structural cause of 18/23 losses given all other gates (EMA, RSI, volume) appear directionally sound.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce signal count significantly but should eliminate the category of 'chase entries far above PDH' that appear to be driving the 0% win rate. Expect 40–60% reduction in signals fired, with the remaining signals concentrated near the actual breakout level.

proposals.panel: Bull Trap Reversal — Failed PDH Breakout (Bearish)
proposals.title: Require the trap candle itself to be a high-volume false breakout spike, not just any close above PDH
proposals.proposed_change: Insert a new gate immediately after the trap_bar is identified (after the existing 'Find the trap bar' loop), before searching for the reversal bar. Compute avg_vol_at_trap = sum(vols[:trap_bar]) / trap_bar if trap_bar > 0 else vols[0]. Then require vols[trap_bar] >= avg_vol_before_trap * TRAP_SPIKE_VOL_RATIO where TRAP_SPIKE_VOL_RATIO = 1.3. If the trap candle itself was not a volume spike, it was not a genuine 'trapped buyers' scenario — it was just a quiet drift above PDH that failed, which has a much lower mean-reversion edge. Add symmetric gate for Bear Trap (bullish): same logic on the breakdown bar. Gate: if vols[trap_bar] < avg_vol_at_trap * TRAP_SPIKE_VOL_RATIO: _dbg_fail(_debug, 'trap_candle_low_volume', symbol, ...); continue.
proposals.reasoning: Bull Trap Reversal has 1 win vs 7 losses vs 15 expired (4.3% win rate, 23 signals). The current code only validates the reversal candle's volume (TRAP_VOL_RATIO), but does not check whether the original false breakout was itself a volume-driven move. A true trap requires trapped participants — those participants only exist in meaningful size if the trap candle drew real buying volume above PDH. Without this gate, the screener is flagging quiet, low-conviction PDH crosses that then drift back below — these are not traps, they are just noise around a level. The 15 expired signals (65% of total) further suggest the setup is not resolving either way, consistent with weak initial participation.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce Bull Trap signal count by an estimated 30–50%, filtering out the low-volume drift-and-fade patterns. Remaining signals should have higher mean-reversion conviction because genuine trapped participants are present. Bear Trap (10.5% win rate, 2W/1L/16E) gets the same improvement but has different failure mode — mostly expiries — so net impact there is less certain.

proposals.panel: ORB — Opening Range Breakout (Bullish and Bearish)
proposals.title: Replace fixed ORB_MAX_RANGE_PCT with ATR-relative opening range gate
proposals.proposed_change: Replace the fixed ORB_MAX_RANGE_PCT = 0.4% gate with an ATR-relative check. Compute atr5 as the 10-period ATR on the 5-min intraday bars from the prior day (last 78 bars of the previous session, using intra5 data already loaded). Then require or_range <= atr5 * ORB_MAX_RANGE_ATR_MULT where ORB_MAX_RANGE_ATR_MULT = 0.5. This means the opening range must be at most 50% of a typical recent 5-min ATR — a genuinely narrow open relative to the stock's own volatility, rather than a fixed 0.4% that is simultaneously too tight for high-volatility stocks (missing valid setups) and too loose for low-volatility stocks (allowing wide relative ranges). Keep ORB_MAX_RANGE_PCT as an absolute cap fallback: or_range_pct > 0.8% always rejects regardless. The new constant ORB_MAX_RANGE_ATR_MULT = 0.5 replaces ORB_MAX_RANGE_PCT as the primary gate.
proposals.reasoning: ORB Bullish has 0 wins in 8 signals (0W/1L/7E), ORB Bearish 0 wins in 1 signal — both tiny samples, so 0% win rate is not statistically actionable on its own. However, the 87.5% expiry rate on ORB Bullish is a structural signal: the setup is finding opening ranges that pass the 0.4% absolute threshold but are not actually narrow relative to the stock's own intraday character, so the breakout lacks the compression needed to generate a directional move. A 0.4% range on a stock with a 0.15% average 5-min ATR is wide; on a stock with a 0.8% ATR it is genuinely tight. The ATR-relative gate is the standard professional implementation of this concept and is the most likely reason the panel is generating setups that expire rather than move.
proposals.expected_impact: Will change which stocks qualify — likely reduces count on high-volatility names with currently-passing wide ranges, and potentially adds some lower-volatility names that were rejected at 0.4% despite being genuinely compressed. Sample is too small to predict win-rate improvement with confidence; primary goal is making the 'narrow' definition stock-specific.

proposals.title: Add intraday VWAP alignment gate — price must be above VWAP at signal time
proposals.proposed_change: After the existing volume gate (day_vol >= PDH_VOL_MIN) and before confidence scoring, add a VWAP alignment check using the same 5-min intraday batch already available. Load intra5 (add _get_5m_batch() call to the function, mirroring the OI Options and ORB panels which already do this). Filter to today_bars5. Compute day VWAP as sum((H+L+C)/3 * V) / sum(V) over all today_bars5. Require current_price > vwap for bullish PDH breakout. Add 'vwap' to result dict. Gate: if current_price <= vwap: _dbg_fail(_debug, 'vwap_alignment', symbol, ...); continue. Introduce constant PDH_REQUIRE_VWAP = True as a flag so it can be disabled for backtesting.
proposals.reasoning: PDH Breakout has 0 wins in 23 signals (18 losses). The OI Options panel already requires VWAP alignment as one of its 5 legs, and that panel's concept — PDH break with trend and momentum — is essentially a subset of what PDH Breakout is trying to do. The current PDH Breakout has no intraday participation filter beyond raw volume count. Stocks that break PDH but are trading below their own day VWAP are doing so on selling pressure against a weak intraday base — the VWAP acts as a real-time institutional participation filter. Given the 0% win rate, adding any meaningful quality filter is likely additive; VWAP is the most data-grounded one already proven in the codebase.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce PDH Breakout signal count by an estimated 25–40% (based on typical intraday VWAP distribution at PDH break time). Cannot guarantee win-rate improvement without backtest, but removes a confirmed category of weak entries — PDH breaks happening below VWAP — that are unlikely to have contributed the 0 wins.
